(2) That tree_fingerprint is cheaper than the walk it replaces — 5.9ms over 806 files (settled.py:66); the before/after read counts are the instrument, not the assumption. (3) That the shake ticket's preprocess contract (fire(name, subjects) -> subset) lands first — depends_on names it; this ticket does not build the contract.

value.missing_check: ONE point not wrapped, on purpose: persisting the last-fire fingerprint across restarts. Today _cleared is in-memory and lost on restart; the fingerprint stamp follows the same rule so a restart walks once — a persisted stamp is instance state under the holder and can come later against a measured need. Everything else is a decision line.

value.better_approach: Considered wiring settled() into each of the 42 walking probes by hand — 42 edits that each new probe must remember; the nest does it once at the shim (Law 4: physics, not policy). Considered a cache inside Probe.fires — that hides the skip from the pulse record; a preprocess sieve stamps skipped_by so the skip is visible in the beat's held list.
value.hidden_assumption: That a probe's trigger depends only on its watched tree — a trigger that reads the clock or the bus would be wrongly settled. Guard: a probe with root=None and no default walk is never settled (always returned by the preprocess sieve); the default root is the repo only for probes that walk it (measured at build: the 48 walkers, their roots named).
